summary: The 200K cameraman clip (6,788 views) is the clear outlier and sets the template: a specific surprising number named in the hook text, the spoken punchline echoed word-for-word as a large subtitle, and a clean two-person reaction shot in blur-fill framing — all resolved in under 25 seconds. The 1,200–1,300 view cluster shares a universal social or physical awkwardness angle (stranger interaction, embarrassing moment, hot take) that needs zero prior context to land. Titles that lead with a concrete detail plus a short payoff phrase consistently beat vague titles. Our one own post at 65 views confirms we have not yet cracked the hook-text pattern of the top clip; this cycle the priority is replicating that specific-number or specific-word on-screen banner. Clips over 25 seconds show no view
moments_to_pick: Cartier says a specific number out loud — a salary, a price, a count — that will surprise a first-time viewer with no context
A stranger physically does something unexpected with Cartier or crew: a challenge, a skill, a confrontation that resolves on camera
An unscripted social exchange goes sideways — flirting lands wrong, someone gets called out, an awkward reveal happens mid-conversation
Cartier coins a made-up or misused word (e.g. 'polyesterous') that sounds quotable and funny pulled out of context
Chat or someone nearby triggers a visible Cartier reaction — shock, dead silence, then laughter — where the reaction IS the clip
A gross or embarrassing physical moment someone immediately tries to explain away with a wild excuse

title_formula: Open with the specific surprising thing (a number, a word, a situation) in plain English, then add the consequence or reaction in 3-6 words, close with one emoji. Never start with 'Cartier2Real' as the first word — lead with the detail. Keep under 70 characters. Example: 'His take on this had the wh
caption_formula: Line 1: One punchy sentence that rewords the hook — do not repeat the title word for word; write it as a reaction or commentary. Line 2: One sentence teasing the payoff from Cartier's perspective or voice without fully spoiling it. Line 3: 'Catch Cartier live on Kick: kick.com/cartier2real' with @ca
avoid: Any establishing shot, slow pan or intro before the punchline — cut to the moment on frame one
Clips over 25 seconds unless a physical or social moment is impossible to understand without the full arc — hard cap at 35s even then
Vague titles with no concrete detail: 'Cartier reacts to something wild' tells the viewer nothing — always name the specific thing
Currency symbols anywhere in titles, captions or on-screen text (campaign rule)
Hook text that is full ALL-CAPS — sentence case on the hook banner matches the top clip and reads better on mobile
Reusing the identical emoji in both the title and the hook banner — vary them
